## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing: Accelerating** 
TrendForce (Sep 30): Q4 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices +10-15% QoQ; PC DRAM +13-18% QoQ; NAND +15-20% QoQ. HBM3E ~$300/stack; HBM4 expected ~$550/stack. No deceleration visible.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk Building** 
All three suppliers aggressively scaling into late 2026: SK Hynix M15X started commercial HBM4 output (1b DRAM); Samsung targeting 250K wafers/mo (+47%); Micron doubling to ~100K wafers/mo by year-end. No fresh correction guidance — but capacity build validates the post-2026 bear case from the baseline thesis.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex: Revised Higher** 
Combined 2026 AI capex now ~$725B (above baseline $600-700B): Amazon $220B, Google $195-205B, Meta $130-145B, Microsoft ~$175B. No guide-down. AWS: "monetizing capacity as fast as we can install it." Bull.

**Signal 4 — AMD/Custom ASICs: Tracking** 
No fresh Oct 3-5 news. AMD MI400/Helios on track for H2 2026, TSMC 2nm, HBM4 (19.6 TB/s). Google Ironwood (TPU v7) and AWS Trainium 3 both GA. Custom ASIC CAGR tracking 44.6%.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics: Coherent + MRVL Catalyst Tomorrow** 
Coherent launched PhotonLink integrated optics platform; InP capacity on pace to double by end 2026 (ahead of schedule). MRVL Investor Day Oct 6 — $18B FY2028 target signals. No InP supply normalization yet — demand still ~2x supply.

**Signal 6 — Solar: Tariff Floor Set; FSLR Beneficiary** 
US Section 232 sets min import prices + 15% tariff on polysilicon/derivatives, effective Dec 4, 2026. Polysilicon (ex-China) ~$17.50/kg; module prices soft ~$0.70/W. FSLR domestic supply chain play; analyst Buy/$310. ENPH Buy/$57.

## Context vs Baseline

AI capex now $725B (baseline: $600-700B) — upside surprise. Memory pricing still accelerating; HBM capacity build by all three suppliers is on pace for late-2026 inflection — the post-2026 correction risk flagged in the baseline is materializing structurally. MU's record results (+379% YoY) confirm the memory supercycle is in full force NOW; the question is whether 2027 sees the anticipated correction as HBM4 supply from all three suppliers hits simultaneously.

## Most Important Development

**Micron (MU) fiscal Q4 2026 blowout**: $54.2B revenue (+379% YoY), 87% gross margin, Q1 FY27 guide of $61.5B confirms the memory supercycle is in full force. Combined with TrendForce's Q4 pricing acceleration, the near-term bull case is intact — but the HBM4 capacity build by all three suppliers into late 2026 is the key watch for 2027 pricing correction risk. MRVL Investor Day tomorrow (Oct 6) is the next near-term catalyst.
